_comment: DECIDE — one picture for context, several WRITTEN options, and he picks one (or Other).
Use it when the alternatives do not exist as pictures yet, or when the difference is not visible: 'open it by default, or leave it closed?' A Yes/No step cannot ask that — yes to which half?
The picture shows how it is TODAY; the options are what could replace it.
title: The settings drawer — how should it open?
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His pick is saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_images: images: where the cropped pictures land. It must contain this file's own name.

runs._comment: runs: one sweep of today's app is all a decide step needs — the options are words, not pictures.

steps._comment: One step is one decision. Two options minimum — one option plus Other is a Yes/No step wearing a disguise.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this decision. It labels his answer.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The drawer that slides in from the left
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there.
steps._comment_crop: crop: the picture of how it is today. Names come from crops.json, or add your own under a top-level "crops" block.
steps.headline: Which section should the settings drawer open on?
steps._comment_headline: headline: the decision itself, in one sentence. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.notice: Whichever you pick is what opens every time you press the settings button.
steps._comment_notice: notice (optional): what rides on the pick.
steps.risk: Every option remembers nothing between sessions; a drawer that remembers is a separate question.
steps._comment_risk: risk (optional): what is true whichever option wins.

highlight._comment: highlight: REQUIRED — one picture means nothing to diff, so you must say what to box. "text" boxes words on screen; a hand-placed "box": [x, y, w, h] is the last resort.

options._comment: One option. Written, not pictured — so pros and cons carry the weight.
options._comment_id: id: your name for this option. It is what his answer records.
options.label: Always the first section
options._comment_label: label: the option's name, two or three words. Never write '(recommended)' into it — set the flag below instead, so the page can badge it.
pros: The same thing is under your thumb every time.
Nothing to learn: the drawer never surprises you.
options._comment_pros: pros: short lines about HIS experience, not the code. One line each.
cons: Two more taps every time the section you want is further down.
options._comment_cons: cons: the same, for what it costs him.
options.summary: The drawer opens the way it does today.
options._comment_summary: summary (optional): a sentence beside the lists, when they need framing.
options._comment_cost: cost: what taking this option costs — work, time, something given up.
options.measured: 0 extra taps to reach the first section
options._comment_measured: measured (optional): a number. Needs a digit in it.
options._comment_recommended: recommended: true on AT MOST ONE option. The page badges it and says why in your summary.

options.label: Wherever you left it
pros: Comes back where you were, which is usually where you are going.
No taps at all when you return to the same section.
cons: The drawer looks different every time you open it.
A section you visited once by mistake keeps coming back.

options.label: A search box first
pros: Anything is two words away, however deep it lives.
cons: Typing to reach a setting you can already see is slower.
The list of sections is pushed down the drawer.
options.cost: A search box, and every setting has to be findable by name.

steps._comment: A second decision, at its smallest: two options, no flags, no numbers.

steps.headline: What should closing the drawer do to an unsaved change?

options.label: Keep it
pros: Nothing you typed is ever lost.
cons: A change you meant to abandon is still there tomorrow.

options.label: Ask you
pros: You decide each time, and nothing goes quietly.
cons: A question every time you close the drawer in a hurry.
